body:
# Constraint Contract

## Status and integration rule

This contract matures constraints only. It does not authorize implementation, alter `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, start Argo, approve a TELOS dossier, certify evidence, or enroll the candidate.

The integration matrix must contain exactly one row for each of `PPC-W01` through `PPC-W29`, with no invented, omitted, duplicated, or grouped obligation. Every row must contain the Daedalus five fields:

`invariant -> enforcement mechanism -> task -> discriminating negative test -> exit criterion`.

A test that merely observes a success string, trusts a committed summary, counts objects without checking their identities, or lets the producer declare its own expected result does not discharge an obligation.

## Smallest complete state model

### Proposal and build lifecycle

The only legal production lifecycle is:

1. `LEGACY_INACTIVE`: all activation conditions are false. Existing legacy behavior and bytes are retained; report `production_profile_evaluated: false`.
2. `ACTIVE_UNPREPARED`: any activation condition is true. No model-backed callback is legal yet.
3. `INPUT_RECORDED`: closed build intent and canonical production input have been written to the proposal artifact store and bound into the signed proposal root.
4. `COMPILED`: a complete pre-build scan and compilation succeeded against current policy, registry, evidence configuration, and disk artifacts.
5. `WORKSHOP_COMPLETE`: models received only the immutable production summary and returned no reserved or controller-owned production identities.
6. `PLANNED`: the controller minted production nodes, attached exact version-2 obligations, and compiled lifecycle metadata into the plan hash.
7. `GATE_PASSED`: a disk-only reconstruction reproduced all current references, sources, obligations, tests, and executable identities and issued the exact version-2 policy certificate.
8. `AUTHORIZED_BUILD`: authorization independently binds that exact plan. Workshop convergence or the candidate compiler cannot create this state.
9. `ORDINARY_SETTLED`: all non-discharge nodes have current signed settlements whose disk artifacts still match.
10. `EVIDENCE_FRONTIER_PREPARED`: required process records and their durable frontier artifact have been made available by the controller boundary.
11. `VERIFICATION_SETTLED`: every discharge node ran its current registered executable and returned zero.
12. `FINAL_PROFILE_PASSED`: final disk-only reclassification exactly matches the authorized production state.
13. `DONE`: generic ledger verification and `done()` confirm every obligation is discharged.

Any blocker or cannot-run result terminates the current invocation. Recovery may resume only from hash-verified durable artifacts. Profile, source, obligation, policy, registry, executable, evidence, or repository-fact drift requires a new planning revision and fresh authorization; it cannot resume the stale plan. A production worker `respec` likewise returns to reconstruction and reauthorization before further dispatch.

The authorization certificate is immutable pre-build evidence. Settlement records never edit, backdate, or replace it.

### Self-publication lifecycle

Each TELOS publication attempt has exactly:

`ABSENT -> PREPARED -> AUTHORIZED -> PUBLISHED`

or

`PREPARED|AUTHORIZED -> SUPERSEDED`.

`PUBLISHED` and `SUPERSEDED` are terminal. Attempt IDs are contiguous controller-derived `attempt-NNN` values. A published attempt precludes a new attempt. Pending or final directories without a matching signed attempt-ledger marker are not trusted.

An unsafe recovery creates an exclusive signed `FORENSIC_HOLD`. While a valid hold exists, every mutating publication, recovery, authorization-recording, preparation, or supersession mode blocks before opening a key. A hold is preserved until a separate Eye/TELOS change-protocol disposition; local deletion or replacement is not recovery.

## Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Trusted input | Untrusted or insufficient input | Required enforcement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eye/controller to compiler | Closed dossier facts, signal resolutions, build mode, evidence bindings | Model prose, inferred defaults, waivers, `n/a` | Closed validation before any model call; contradiction checks; no lowering |
| Process to repository | Explicit physical repository root and safe relative paths | CWD defaults, host ignore files, absolute semantic paths, escaping links | Stable bounded reads, realpath containment, race detection, deterministic traversal |
| Artifact store | Canonical content-addressed bytes and signed ledger references | In-memory dossier, mutable current view, filename identity alone | Re-read and re-hash at proposal gate, check execution, restart, and settlement |
| Scanner to profile | Registered structured facts and exact current signal resolutions | Arbitrary text matches, unknown dependency semantics | Monotonic joins; unresolved signals block; partial scans are discarded |
| Policy and registry | Checked-in canonical policy and current closed registry source closure | Remote packs, caller commands, caller implementation refs, host expected results | Versioned closed loaders and current reference derivation |
| Workshop/model output | Ordinary implementation tasks within permitted writes | Production sources, verification IDs, skips, policy choices, controller artifacts | Read-only summary, reserved-ID rejection, protected-write rejection, controller minting |
| Runtime adapter | Literal loopback routes and synthetic fixture bindings | DNS, redirects, proxies, external URLs, adapter-declared outcomes | Registry-owned limits and policy-owned expected transitions |
| Structural evidence | Bounded JSON and exact current source hashes | Prose, self-declared pass, unsupported YAML/HCL/Terraform | Exactly one matching control and registry-owned predicates |
| Process evidence | Public Ed25519 keyring and signed current record | Unsigned declaration, private key, stale or cross-plan record | Exact signature, source/check/plan/build/freshness verification |
| Build ledger to process evidence | Recomputed plan, authorized signed ordinary settlements, current disk trees | Plan intent alone or ledger-declared tree hash alone | Independently derived `executing_build_ref` |
| Authorization to execution | Certificate matching recomputed plan and required contract version | Caller-selected certificate version or stale plan hash | Plan-aware V1/V2 dispatch and repeated authorization checks |
| Candidate to TELOS dogfood | Ordinary host lifecycle with separately approved dossier and plan | Repository-name branch, old packet fixture, committed summary, direct ledger insertion | Same compiler, registry, gate, scanner, checks, settlement, and `done()` path |
| Public claims | Executed predicates and exact evidence references | Marketing prose or broad compliance/security claims | Closed claim vocabulary plus explicit non-claims |

The controller and build controller remain one trust principal in version 1. Content addressing does not prove human authorship of the dossier.

## Normative schema law

All versioned objects are closed: exact keys, exact value domains, no `additionalProperties`, no duplicate JSON keys, no prototype keys, no unsafe integers, no unpaired surrogates, and no implicit defaults. Set-valued arrays are duplicate-free and sorted with a code-unit comparator. `"none"` is exclusive where allowed. A schema extension requires an explicit contract/version decision and tests; an unknown version or field fails closed.

The exact frozen schemas are normative for:

- production input and evidence configuration;
- signal resolutions, semantic facts, and scanner signals;
- policy, detector, condition, projection, and template objects;
- production source records and version-2 obligations;
- production lifecycle metadata and policy certificate V2;
- registry metadata, check parameters, runtime manifest, structural controls, keyrings, and process records;
- build intent and proposal root references;
- evidence-config sidecar, process frontier result/artifact, and settlement result;
- TELOS attempt ledger records, approval/authorization snapshots, publication manifests, and forensic holds.

The allowed policy operators are exactly `all`, `any`, `not`, `eq`, `contains`, `intersects`, `gte`, and `lte`. Templates replace only whole values equal to `$profile`, `$evidence`, or `$obligation_id`.

The policy catalog is exactly these 31 IDs:

`AI-CLAIM-001`, `AI-DECISION-001`, `AI-EGRESS-001`, `AI-LINEAGE-001`, `AI-OPS-001`, `AI-OUTPUT-001`, `AI-PROVIDER-001`, `AI-RAG-001`, `AI-TENANT-001`, `AI-TOOL-001`, `AUTHN-001`, `AUTHN-002`, `AUTHZ-001`, `AUTHZ-002`, `DATA-001`, `DATA-002`, `DELIVERY-001`, `DELIVERY-002`, `OBS-001`, `OBS-002`, `PAY-001`, `PAY-002`, `PRIV-001`, `PRIV-002`, `PRIV-003`, `RECOVERY-001`, `RECOVERY-002`, `SCALE-001`, `SCALE-002`, `SUPPLY-001`, and `SUPPLY-002`.

The registry contains exactly these eight kinds:

`production-loopback-http-v1`, `production-auth-boundary-v1`, `production-tenant-isolation-v1`, `production-rate-limit-v1`, `production-webhook-v1`, `production-ai-egress-v1`, `production-json-assertions-v1`, and `production-record-v1`.

No production parameter schema accepts command, script, interpreter, argument-vector, working-directory, environment, shell, executable, external URL, expected-result, source-ref, check-contract-ref, or implementation-ref injection.

## Content-address and executable law

`H(value)` means SHA-256 over the shared canonical JSON encoding. Every consumer must recompute references from current canonical bytes; comparing a stored reference to another stored reference is insufficient.

The mandatory identities are:

- `production_input_ref = H(canonical production input)`;
- `profile_ref = H({ compiler_contract, compiled_profile })`;
- `repo_facts_ref = H({ facts_version, sorted semantic facts, sorted resolved signals })`;
- `policy_ref = H(canonical policy)` and rule-local `rule_ref`;
- `parameter_schema_ref` over schema, guards, limits, result semantics, and execution environment contract;
- `implementation_ref` over exact registered implementation and transitive execution-source closure;
- `registry_ref` over the sorted closed registry metadata;
- `runtime_manifest_ref` over the validated manifest or exactly `null`;
- `process_keyring_ref` over the canonical public keyring or exactly `null`;
- `evidence_config_ref` over canonical evidence plus manifest/keyring references;
- source refs over the complete production source identity;
- `obligation_set_ref = H(sorted production source refs)`;
- production check contract V2 over version, kind, canonical parameters, and current implementation ref;
- legacy obligation/check/executable preimages exactly unchanged;
- production executable identity including `env_contract` when present;
- `plan_hash` over all production lifecycle references, sources, obligations, tests, and metadata;
- `executing_build_ref` over current signed ordinary settlements and independently re-hashed disk artifacts;
- frontier, settlement, publication, and signed-record refs over their complete canonical bodies, never self-referential fields.

A global profile, policy, registry, or evidence change invalidates `plan_hash`. An unrelated rule or profile field must not rewrite a verification node whose local projections and implementation are unchanged.

## Failure semantics

Compiler/CLI exits are exact:

- `0`: the requested predicate succeeded; advisory escalation may be present;
- `2`: deterministic controller-remediable blocker, contradiction, unsupported evidence, unresolved classification, mismatch, or drift;
- `1`: execution cannot be trusted, including I/O/race/path failure, malformed built-in policy, registry failure, unsafe traversal, or internal failure.

Cannot-run takes precedence over blockers. No nonzero compiler invocation replaces an existing output.

Check exits are exact: `0` proved, `1` assertion ran and failed, `2` could not run safely or received invalid input. Generic ledger handling blocks every nonzero result while preserving the distinction.

The finding-code set is the frozen design set. `PROFILE_ESCALATED` is advisory only. Proposal routing is immutable:

- hold, non-reparable, human-required: profile/lifecycle/schema/contradiction/classification/stale-resolution and evidence-adapter/format blockers;
- verification, reparable, no human required: `BLOCKED_PROFILE_DRIFT`;
- protocol, non-reparable: policy/version, check registration/contract, source, obligation, and lifecycle mismatches;
- unrecoverable: scanner safety/limit and `CANNOT_RUN`.

A protocol or unrecoverable result cannot route to revise or authorized. Activated `production_profile` certificate status is only `pass` or `fail`, never `n/a`.

## Proof obligations and discriminating negative controls

### PPC-W01 — Authority remains external and hash-exact

No implementation task may begin without TELOS authorization over the exact matured-plan bytes and successful Argo entry against that authority. Workshop convergence, design approval, comprehension labels, self-hosting, or candidate output grants no authority. This run must not alter `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`.

**Negative control:** change one byte of the matured plan after producing an otherwise valid authorization packet. The authority/entry verifier must reject it before any task callback, code edit, or slice ledger event.

### PPC-W02 — Activation is complete and pre-model

Activation is true iff proposal lifecycle is true, market-bound is true, or either production field is present. Every active build requires proposal lifecycle and a complete profile before any model, workshop, council, team, convention-detection, or decomposition call. All-false legacy behavior remains byte-compatible.

**Negative control:** invoke each activation trigger with a missing profile and instrument every external callback. The result must include the exact lifecycle/profile blocker and every callback count must remain zero; the all-false control must still enter the legacy path.

### PPC-W03 — Controller input is closed, factual, and secret-free

Only controller input may set profile facts, signal resolutions, policy selection, or evidence bindings. All profile cross-field rules, path rules, identifier limits, exclusivity rules, and secret/personal-data rejection from the frozen schema are mandatory. There is no waiver, unknown-accepted, free-text skip, or model-authored applicability field.

**Negative control:** add one unknown key, secret-shaped value, contradictory `none`, or out-of-scope data class to an otherwise valid dossier. Validation must fail with no canonical input artifact and no model call.

### PPC-W04 — Canonicalization is deterministic and nonconstant

Equivalent semantic inputs produce byte-identical artifacts and references on Node 18 and 20 regardless of object order, set order, traversal creation order, locale, clock, absolute root, or path separator. A semantic one-bit change changes every identity whose preimage contains it.

**Negative control:** compile permuted equivalent fixtures on both Node versions and require exact byte equality, then change one relevant scalar and require the profile and global plan references to differ. A constant or host-dependent hash fails.

### PPC-W05 — Artifact I/O is durable, contained, and reconstruction-only

Controller artifacts are stable-read, size-bounded, physically contained, canonical, content-addressed, atomically installed, and fsynced. Proposal verification and settlement use disk artifacts, never caller-supplied mutable replacements. Current-view files are conveniences, not trust anchors. Controller artifacts and trust anchors are never model write targets.

**Negative control:** force a file identity/mtime change between pre-read and post-read while a sentinel output exists. The operation must return cannot-run, expose no partial parsed value, leave the sentinel byte-identical, and reject an in-memory substitute.

### PPC-W06 — Repository scanning is bounded and all-or-nothing

The scanner is read-only, network-free, deterministic, limited to registered files/detectors, and immune to host ignore suppression. It rejects physical escapes, unsafe aliases, required unreadable files, changed-during-read files, malformed registered data, and byte limits. A cannot-run scan contributes no partial facts.

**Negative control:** place a registered manifest behind an escaping symlink after another file has already emitted a fact. The result must be cannot-run with an empty accepted fact set, not a partial profile.

### PPC-W07 — Observation reconciliation is monotonic and signal-exact

Structured confirmed observations may union sets, raise ordered floors, or change false capabilities to true. They never lower declarations. Textual detections remain signals until an exact current controller resolution exists. Duplicate, fabricated, missing, or stale resolutions block. Non-ordered inventory contradictions block rather than selecting a convenient minimum.

**Negative control:** declare external exposure and supply a lower internal observation while also providing a resolution for a previous signal hash. Exposure must remain external and the stale resolution must produce `STALE_SIGNAL_RESOLUTION`; neither condition may suppress obligations.

### PPC-W08 — Policy and catalog are pinned, closed, and complete

The built-in canonical policy is the only V1 policy. It contains exactly the 31 IDs, eleven domains, frozen tiers/kinds/triggers, and required result `pass`. Conditions and projections are closed data. Every rule has a nearest non-trigger, one-fact trigger, pass, fail, and stale-identity fixture. Host evidence cannot choose expected outcomes.

**Negative control:** independently remove one catalog rule and replace one operator with an unknown operator. Exact catalog equality and policy loading must fail; counting the remaining rules or evaluating the unknown operator as false is not acceptable.

### PPC-W09 — Evidence applicability is exact and tiered

Each triggered obligation declares exactly one of runtime, structural, or process evidence. Missing adapters, operations, paths, formats, or keyrings produce typed blockers without omitting the obligation. Reports describe only the proved tier. Evidence configuration and trust-anchor bytes are hash-bound before authorization.

**Negative control:** trigger a runtime obligation while configuring `runtime.kind: none` and providing a structural file claiming success. Compilation must retain the runtime obligation and return `EVIDENCE_ADAPTER_REQUIRED`; no report may promote the structural file to runtime proof.

### PPC-W10 — Registry execution is closed and implementation-bound

The current registry contains exactly eight kinds. Parameter schemas, guards, limits, status semantics, scrubbed environment contract, dispatcher, runner, redactor, entry modules, and transitive helpers are implementation-bound. Callers cannot select executables or expected outcomes. Every production node resolves to exact bare `node` plus `telos-scrubbed-v1`; the absolute controller runtime path exists only at spawn.

**Negative control:** replace a registered implementation body or status mapper with a passing no-op while retaining the old stored contract. Gate re-resolution must produce `CHECK_CONTRACT_STALE` or executable mismatch and must not run or discharge the stale node.

### PPC-W11 — Runtime evidence is bounded loopback behavior

Runtime checks accept only literal `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` HTTP endpoints, explicit ports, closed operations, synthetic fixtures, fixed limits, no redirects, no DNS, no proxies, and no external sockets. Policy owns statuses and state transitions; the manifest owns route mapping only. An adapter must trace invocation of the candidate semantic handler.

**Negative control:** mutate an otherwise valid adapter to return the expected status without invoking the candidate handler and redirect one request to an external hostname. The check must return cannot-run or assertion-failed, and the external/fake transport count must remain zero.

### PPC-W12 — Structural evidence proves only exact machine artifacts

Structural checks read bounded JSON only, require exactly one matching control across configured artifacts, verify every source path and current byte hash, and apply registry-owned obligation predicates. Evidence cannot declare its own pass criterion or cite itself. Unsupported formats remain blocked.

**Negative control:** duplicate a favorable control in a second artifact or change a referenced source byte without updating its hash. The check must fail/cannot-run rather than select one control or trust the declared hash.

### PPC-W13 — Process evidence is externally signed and execution-bound

A process record must use the closed schema, canonical signature preimage, authorized public Ed25519 key, exact obligation/source/check/plan/executing-build identities, exact source hashes, required outcome, and freshness window. Private keys are never repository artifacts. Missing, expired, malformed, cross-plan, or conflicting current records cannot discharge an obligation.

**Negative control:** replay a valid signed pass record against a different plan or mutate an ordinary artifact after settlement. Recomputed `executing_build_ref` must differ and the record check must return cannot-run; a conflicting current fail record must not be ignored.

### PPC-W14 — Production obligations are typed V2 without legacy drift

Production policy sources use only explicit obligation version 2 and `source_kind: production-policy`; they are never fabricated concerns. Unknown versions/source kinds fail. Legacy obligations omit the version field and retain their exact historical preimages, contract refs, executable refs, and obligation-free plan bytes.

**Negative control:** encode a production source as a legacy concern and encode a legacy obligation with explicit version 1. Both must fail, while the pinned legacy golden hashes remain byte-identical.

### PPC-W15 — Every obligation reconciles bijectively to one source

Every production obligation maps to exactly one current compiler source and every legacy obligation to exactly one reconstructed concern. Source class, ID, source ref, contract, result, discharge node, test, executable, and `verifies` registration must agree. Missing, extra, duplicate, orphan, or cross-bound entries block.

**Negative control:** duplicate one production source while deleting a different source so total counts remain unchanged. Exact-set reconciliation must report source/obligation mismatch; count equality or map overwrite cannot pass.

### PPC-W16 — Production verification nodes remain controller-owned

Models receive a deep-frozen summary only. The controller alone mints stable reserved IDs, empty writes, policy-derived reads, exact requirements, current registry tests, and dependencies on every captured ordinary task plus explicit evidence producers. Review obligations may add but never replace production obligations.

**Negative control:** return workshop output containing `verify-production-ai-egress-001` or a write to the process keyring. The proposal must fail before graph compilation; renaming, shadowing, or treating it as a review node is forbidden.

### PPC-W17 — Plan and certificate bind the complete production state

Production lifecycle metadata is all-or-nothing and binds input, profile, semantic facts, policy, registry, evidence, source set, compiled artifact, obligations, tests, and lifecycle metadata into `plan_hash`. Production plans require policy certificate V2 with `production_profile: pass`; V1 and `n/a` cannot authorize them.

**Negative control:** change only `evidence_config_ref` while replaying the old plan hash and V2 certificate. Recomputed plan/certificate verification must fail; changing the reference without changing authorization cannot pass.

### PPC-W18 — Proposal verification rejects stale disk state

The proposal gate restarts from the signed proposal root and content-addressed disk artifacts, re-runs current scanning/compilation, and re-resolves current policy, registry, source, check, and executable identities. Caller dossier state, current-view state, or a committed summary cannot substitute. Every referenced artifact must be re-hashed from bytes.

**Negative control:** keep a valid in-memory compiled object while replacing the disk production-input artifact or registry helper byte. Disk-only verification must fail with the corresponding lifecycle/check mismatch and issue no certificate.

### PPC-W19 — Failure reporting is closed and precedence-safe

Reports use only frozen finding codes, closed severity/status shapes, bounded redacted detail, exact exit codes, and immutable proposal routing. Cannot-run dominates blocker; advisory escalation does not become a certificate finding. Nonzero paths do not replace successful artifacts or route to authorization.

**Negative control:** produce a blocker and a scanner I/O failure in one invocation with a sentinel output. Exit must be `1`, include cannot-run detail without leaked payload, leave the sentinel unchanged, and never report authorized/revise.

### PPC-W20 — Settlement requires current execution and every discharge

The executing build is derived from the recomputed plan, authorized signed ordinary-node ledger records, and independently re-hashed disk artifacts. Every production check must exit zero, every obligation must be registered against the exact test, and generic ledger verification plus `done()` must reject any undischarged obligation. Exit `1` and `2` remain distinct but both block.

**Negative control:** mutate one ordinary artifact after its signed settlement and make one discharge test exit `1` while another exits `2`. Executing-build derivation and `done()` must block; structured results must preserve both statuses rather than treating either as pass.

### PPC-W21 — Final facts and respec invalidate stale authority

Immediately before final settlement, the controller re-runs disk-only scanning and compilation, including untracked declared outputs. Any changed expected profile, source, obligation, check, executable, evidence, or lifecycle identity returns `BLOCKED_PROFILE_DRIFT`. A production `respec` cannot mutate and continue under the old certificate.

**Negative control:** introduce a newly confirmed provider dependency during the build. Final verification must return `BLOCKED_PROFILE_DRIFT`, dispatch no further settlement success, preserve the old certificate unchanged, and require a newly planned/authorized revision.

### PPC-W22 — Process frontier is durable and non-certifying

After ordinary settlement and before discharge execution, the controller must either verify an exact existing frontier artifact or invoke the explicit process-evidence frontier once. The frontier binds plan, executing build, configured record paths, and exact raw record bytes but does not certify record semantics. Missing callbacks, partial evidence, stale artifacts, unauthorized writes, or callback exceptions block before discharge.

**Negative control:** restart with a frontier artifact whose plan hash is current but whose evidence file changed by one byte. The artifact must not be reused or overwritten, the callback must not silently repair it, and no discharge node may run.

### PPC-W23 — All activated consumers and fresh hosts use one lifecycle

Every genuine market-bound or proposal-lifecycle consumer, including both forges, routes through production preparation and V2 proposal authorization. Readiness helpers remain explicitly non-authorizing. A neutral fresh host needs no TELOS authority or institutional-memory files; absent triggered evidence produces typed blockers rather than dropped obligations.

**Negative control:** run a market-bound forge with green readiness packets but no profile and instrument legacy gate/model calls; it must block before them. Separately compile a minimal neutral host without `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`, then trigger an unsupported adapter and require the exact evidence blocker.

### PPC-W24 — The bank-style demonstration proves the bounded negative path

The committed demonstration must traverse the real compiler, plan, proposal gate, checks, settlement, and `done()` path using only `000-00-0000` labeled invalid synthetic data and a loopback fake provider. It must prove unsafe egress fails, corrected egress blocks before transport and emits redacted audit data, and profile escalation changes obligations and invalidates authorization.

**Negative control:** verify the committed unsafe, corrected, and escalated cases from source artifacts rather than trusting the summary. Any outbound payload, unredacted marker, unchanged plan hash, or missing new tenant/payment obligation fails verification.

### PPC-W25 — TELOS self-hosting has no privileged path

TELOS uses a controller-approved tracked dossier and separately authorized self-host plan through the same ordinary compiler, policy, registry, proposal reconstruction, V2 certificate, loopback/synthetic checks, final scan, ledger discharge, and `done()` path. The historical packet-only fixture and repository identity are insufficient. The run restarts from disk and leaves the tracked checkout clean.

**Negative control:** independently delete an obligation, substitute a no-op check, lower confirmed egress/write/execute, and add a confirmed provider fact. Each isolated mutation must produce its expected blocker; changing the repository name must not change the verdict.

### PPC-W26 — Self-publication attempts are immutable, signed, and recoverable only by the closed protocol

Controller, process, and attempt-governance keys are distinct external Ed25519 keys. Attempt artifacts are write-once; the signed append-only attempt ledger is the commit marker. Prefixes, transitions, IDs, keyring refs, and publication manifests are re-verified. Crash recovery follows the closed pending/final/marker table. Unsafe recovery creates a durable forensic hold and cannot be converted into supersession or success.

**Negative control:** inject crashes at each directory/ledger fsync and rename boundary, then create a marker/bytes mismatch. Recovery must enter cannot-run, record a valid forensic hold, and all later mutating modes must block before key access; deleting or forging the hold must not restore operation.

### PPC-W27 — Runtime and host portability are fail-closed

New runtime code is Node 18/20 ESM with only `node:` and repository-relative imports and zero dependencies. It performs no shell invocation, command assembly, ambient credential propagation, live-provider call, or real-personal-data use. Physical paths are portable and contained. Production children receive only the ten-key scrubbed environment allowlist and the controller runtime executable.

**Negative control:** place a fake `node` first in `PATH`, set credential/proxy/canary environment variables, and mutate one audited module to import an external package. Production execution must use the injected controller runtime, expose none of the canaries, make no external request, and the import audit must reject the dependency.

### PPC-W28 — Lifecycle evidence and enrollment ordering are executable

Commit-anchored evidence must exist for canonical Iliad pre-review, parallel Daedalus parentage and exact obligation coverage, TELOS authorization of the matured hash, Argo comprehension and append-only slices, reference documentation, committed TELOS self-hosting, Clotho weave, Iliad post-review, retrospective, and contract verification before enrollment. Superseded evidence remains preserved. Enrollment and dogfood claims cannot precede the required green self-run.

**Negative control:** remove or stale-bind the retrospective, self-hosting publication, one Daedalus parent, or one required slice event while leaving enrollment present. Institutional verification must fail; prose enrollment or an acceptance summary cannot repair the missing lineage.

### PPC-W29 — Claims do not exceed executable predicates

Machine summaries and institutional contracts may claim only exact bounded predicates re-derived from referenced artifacts. They must preserve the runtime/structural/process distinctions and all explicit non-claims. No result may claim legal compliance, certification, universal security, operational effectiveness, complete discovery, fairness, accuracy, availability, or future-host success.

**Negative control:** add an unknown public claim ID or change a summary from bounded runtime-fixture success to `secure`, `compliant`, or `certified` while retaining the same evidence refs. The publication/institutional verifier must reject the claim; a signature over the broader prose is not proof.

## Exit condition for constraint preservation

Constraint verification may return literal `preserved` only if the integrated matrix is a strict bijection over the 29 IDs, every enforcement mechanism is controller-owned where required, every row names an executable negative test with the stated failing outcome, and no row weakens a frozen schema, hash preimage, failure state, evidence tier, authority boundary, or non-claim. Any missing row, broader claim, hidden skip, self-certified result, stale-reference comparison, or open schema is `violated` and routes to The Eye.
